propositions: The false_accept computation at parity.py:81 inverts the actual false-positive rate by counting not-blocked safe items instead of blocked safe items, making it a specificity metric (higher-is-better) but consuming it as an error rate (lower-is-better).

The gate criterion at parity.py:125 fails candidates for false-firing LESS than baseline and at parity.py:252 the max_false_accept ceiling of 0.10 is effectively always-fail because specificity is far above 0.10, causing the frontier slot of the recorded Bedrock provider-parity run to fail incorrectly on two gold-ADVISORY cases.

The false_accept metric must be corrected to count blocked safe items (decision == "block" over label != "block") rather than not-blocked safe items, making it align with the established meaning in eval.py:399-491 and the release threshold documentation.

The correct false-accept computation yields the frontier slot's false-accept value as 0.071 (improvement) instead of 0.929 (reported regression), which clears the non-inferiority gate that was previously failing with "false-accept rose 0.143".

The fixture at fidelity_spot_eval.py mislabels conflict blocks as "advisory" (gold-safe) when the comment states they must be blocked, which was only survivable under the inverted metric and must be corrected to reflect the actual intent.

The fix requires updating the docstring at parity.py:71-72 and verifying both consumption sites maintain their greater-than comparison direction while becoming correct for the error rate interpretation.
